title: gRNAde — RNA sequence design for a target structure
description: Design candidate RNA sequences for a target 3D structure (inverse folding). Outputs are candidates for the supplied backbone — a successful run does not validate folding or biological function.
citation: Joshi et al., gRNAde: Geometric Deep Learning for 3D RNA inverse design. https://github.com/chaitjo/geometric-rna-design

fields.name: structure
fields.label: Input structure
fields.help: One PDB file with a single RNA chain.

fields.name: chain
fields.label: RNA chain
fields.help: Auto-detected if the structure has a single RNA chain.

example_summary: A tiny synthetic 6-nucleotide RNA backbone (chain A), bundled so you can try the pipeline without hunting for a structure.
example_details: This is a hand-made placeholder fixture, not a real biological molecule: six residues (A-U-G-C-A-U) on a single RNA chain with just enough atoms to exercise parsing, chain detection, and the end-to-end run. gRNAde's job is 'inverse folding' — given a 3D backbone shape, propose RNA sequences predicted to fold into it. For this example the backbone is synthetic, so the returned sequences are only meaningful as a demonstration of the workflow. Swap in a real PDB (one RNA chain) to design for an actual target. On the fake backend (no GPU) all sequences are deterministic placeholders; real gRNAde designs come from the Runpod endpoint whose image bakes the checkpoint (see deploy-docs/GRNADE_DEPLOY.md).
notes: Real runner landed (worker/run_grnade.py: checkpoint-gated real path via upstream's programmatic API; raises on failure, fails loudly without the checkpoint). source_commit is verified from GitHub (gRNAde v1.0 release 2025-12-15) but build-unverified; checkpoint_digest, worker_image_digest, max_sequence_length and structure max_bytes stay provisional until a real Runpod smoke run. Code license MIT; the one gRNAde checkpoint (chaitjo/gRNAde on HF) is MIT, but the HF repo also bundles rhofold/ribonanzanet weights under their own LICENSE files — verify those before redistributing an image. Adapter exposes raw sampled designs (temperature 0.1) and deliberately omits upstream's RibonanzaNet scoring/filtering loop; upstream-parity is checked against gRNAde.sample, not design.py's filtered CSV.
